title: UART Deep Dive
subtitle: Hardware and software serial, GPS modules, and RS-232
author: Kernal Team

whyItExists.problem: Many real-world peripherals use UART as their communication interface: GPS modules, GSM/4G modems, Bluetooth serial modules (HC-05), fingerprint scanners, and industrial sensors. Without understanding UART wiring and baud rate matching, you can't use these devices.
whyItExists.solution: UART is a point-to-point asynchronous serial protocol using just TX and RX wires. Understanding frame format, baud rates, flow control, and the difference between hardware vs software UART lets you connect any UART-based device reliably.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Connecting GPS modules, GSM modems, Bluetooth modules (HC-05/HC-06), RFID readers, fingerprint sensors, barcode scanners, and any device with a TTL serial interface.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Multi-device buses (use I2C or SPI). Long distances in noisy industrial environments (use RS-485, CAN bus). High-speed streaming (use USB or Ethernet).

explainModes.beginner: UART is the most basic way two chips talk to each other. One wire goes from TX (transmit) on one chip to RX (receive) on the other, and vice versa. They agree on a speed (baud rate) in advance and that's it — no clock wire needed.
explainModes.simple: UART sends characters one bit at a time. The TX pin is normally HIGH; to send a byte, it pulls LOW (start bit), sends 8 data bits, then goes HIGH (stop bit). Both devices must be set to the same baud rate or you'll get garbage.
explainModes.standard: UART frame: 1 start bit (LOW), 5–8 data bits (LSB first), optional parity bit (even/odd), 1–2 stop bits (HIGH). The baud rate determines bit period (e.g., 9600 baud = 104 µs/bit). Devices must be within ±3% of each other. TX of one device connects to RX of the other.
explainModes.technical: The ATmega328P USART has a 16-bit baud rate generator: UBRR = F_CPU / (16 × baud) - 1. HardwareSerial uses 64-byte ring buffers and UART_RX / UART_TX interrupts. SoftwareSerial bit-bangs timing using delayMicroseconds(), disabling global interrupts during bit reception.
explainModes.deepDive: RS-232 (DB9 connector on old PCs) uses ±12V levels — a MAX232 converts to TTL 0/5V. RS-485 (balanced differential pair) extends to 1200 metres at 100 kbps and supports 32+ devices. ModBus RTU is an industrial protocol layered on RS-485. UART with hardware flow control (RTS/CTS) prevents buffer overflow on high-throughput connections.

content.text: UART is the foundation of serial communication — simple, robust, and ubiquitous. Unlike I2C or SPI, it needs no clock wire: devices agree on a speed (baud rate) in advance and each generates its own clock. The only wires needed are TX (transmit), RX (receive), and a shared GND. Always cross-connect: TX of device A → RX of device B.

content.code:
UART Frame Format (8N1 — most common)
───────────────────────────────────────
  Idle  │Start│ D0 │ D1 │ D2 │ D3 │ D4 │ D5 │ D6 │ D7 │Stop│  Idle
  HIGH  │ LOW │ b0 │ b1 │ b2 │ b3 │ b4 │ b5 │ b6 │ b7 │HIGH│  HIGH

8N1 = 8 data bits, No parity, 1 stop bit
Baud 9600 = 1 bit every 104 µs → 1 byte = 10 bits = 1.04 ms
Baud 115200 = 1 bit every 8.7 µs → 1 byte = 86.8 µs

a.name: Hardware UART
a.description: Dedicated USART peripheral in the MCU
strengths: Reliable at all baud rates up to 2 Mbps
weaknesses: Limited count: Uno has 1 (pins 0/1), shared with USB
a.useWhen: Any UART device on a board with spare hardware UART pins

b.name: SoftwareSerial
b.description: Bit-bangs UART timing on any GPIO pins
strengths: Free up hardware UART for USB debug
weaknesses: Conflicts with Servo, DHT, encoder libs
b.useWhen: Uno with no spare hardware UART — but prefer Mega or ESP32 for multi-serial

content.text: GPS modules like the Neo-6M and Neo-M8N output NMEA sentences at 9600 baud over UART. Each line starts with a sentence identifier ($GPGGA, $GPRMC) containing latitude, longitude, altitude, and time. The TinyGPS++ library parses these automatically.

GPS modules need an unobstructed view of the sky to get a fix. Place the antenna near a window or outdoors. The first fix (cold start) can take 30–60 seconds. Once fixed, subsequent locks are faster (warm start ~5 s).
Two Arduinos can communicate directly over UART by connecting TX of one to RX of the other and sharing GND. This is useful for splitting a project across two boards.

When connecting a 5V Arduino UART to a 3.3V device (ESP32, Raspberry Pi), the 5V TX signal from Arduino will damage the 3.3V device's RX pin. Use a voltage divider (1 kΩ + 2 kΩ) or a logic-level converter on the TX→RX line. The 3.3V TX → 5V RX direction is usually fine (3.3V exceeds the HIGH threshold on most 5V AVR inputs).

questions.question: How do you correctly wire two UART devices together?
options: Connect TX of both devices together
Connect TX of device A to RX of device B, and TX of B to RX of A
Connect all four pins: TX-TX, RX-RX, SCK-SCK, SS-SS
Only one wire is needed — they share a common clock
questions.explanation: UART is cross-connected: transmit (TX) from one device goes to receive (RX) of the other. Both devices also need a shared GND.

questions.question: What is the key advantage of hardware UART over SoftwareSerial?
options: Hardware UART runs in background using interrupts, without blocking other code
Hardware UART has a longer range
questions.explanation: Hardware UART uses a dedicated USART peripheral with interrupt-driven ring buffers. It runs independently of the CPU. SoftwareSerial must disable interrupts during bit reception, potentially corrupting other time-sensitive operations.

questions.question: A GPS module outputs data at 9600 baud but you read nothing. What should you check first?
options: Whether TX of the GPS is connected to RX of Arduino (not TX-to-TX)
The I2C address of the GPS
Whether the Serial Monitor is set to 9600 baud
questions.explanation: The most common UART wiring mistake is TX-to-TX or RX-to-RX. UART is cross-connected: GPS TX → Arduino RX, GPS RX → Arduino TX. Also verify baud rates match.

faq.a: RS-232 is an older serial standard using ±12V logic levels (±12V for HIGH/LOW vs 0/5V TTL). It uses a DB9 or DB25 connector, common on older industrial equipment. A MAX232 chip converts between RS-232 and TTL levels. Modern microcontrollers use TTL UART; RS-232 is mainly for interfacing with legacy equipment.

faq.q: How do I read a full line from UART without blocking?
faq.a: Build a character-by-character buffer: append each received character to a String or char[], and when you receive '\n' (newline), process the complete line. Avoid readStringUntil('\n') in time-sensitive code as it blocks until the delimiter arrives or timeout.

faq.q: My GPS shows no fix after 10 minutes. What's wrong?
faq.a: Common causes: (1) indoors or obstructed sky — move near a window or outside; (2) no antenna connected; (3) cold start after long storage — may take up to 15 minutes; (4) UART wiring error — check TX→RX cross-connection. Use Serial.print(gps.charsProcessed()) to verify data is arriving.
